checks: Every label’s p_i belongs to D, is the unique u_i maximum, and has strictly positive score. Every different point strictly above the negative cut plane is interior to a nontrivial cone segment unless it is the apex, so any other extreme point has strictly negative score.

A finite extreme-point representation of zero exists by the face induction. Omitting one of the distinct apices makes its selected normal evaluate strictly negative at the represented point. Carathéodory thus bounds the number by d+1.

At equality the positive representation uses all apices and is affinely independent by weight elimination. Subtracting the maximal t_i/α_i times the balanced affine representation of zero makes all other coefficients nonpositive, giving the through-zero cover and exhausting all extreme points.

With positive normal balance, a nonnegative score occurs at every point. This gives the cover directly, and projecting all vertices to the normal span keeps them distinct and individually necessary in any representation of zero. Carathéodory in that span forces rank d.
